The boiling point of water at sea level is usually expressed in degrees Celsius. In this case, it is 140-250 degrees Fahrenheit. However, in reality, the boiling point is much lower than that of air or water, and has a tendency to be hotter than the atmosphere. When the temperature rises above freezing, it causes the boiling point to rise. This means that when the temperature reaches -68 ° C (73.9 ° F), the boiling point rises. A thermometer reading of 140-150 ° C (78.9 ° F) is used to determine the boiling point of water at sea level.

Maria and her colleagues develop a new species of corals called the Great Barrier Reef. The team has three years of research to help us understand how these remarkable reefs are formed.
Dr. Maria is the project manager at the Institute for Tropical Marine Research in The University of Queensland. She researches reef ecology with the Australian National Coral Reef Program (ANCOS). She also researches how marine life forms form under similar conditions in their environment. Her latest project focuses on an important aspect of coral reef biology: coral bleaching.
She is a professor at the University of Queensland. She conducts research on coral bleaching – both in Australia and around the world. She is based at the University of Queensland.
Dr. Maria is the author of two papers published by the Institute for Tropical Marine Research (ANCOS) that are part of the Australian Academy of Science. Dr. Maria was born in 1970. She is the author of three books of essays. She is a graduate student in environmental science.
